subject: Re: Redwood Inference - Post-call recap, stakeholder mapping & procurement next steps
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme-health.com>

Cc: Priya Rao <priya.roa@acme-health.com>, Nina Ortiz <nina.ortiz@acme-health.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Redwood Inference - Intro & discovery follow-up

Thanks for the call this morning, Aditya — good overview. A quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying questions: 

- Stakeholders: confirmed internally that the economic buyer is Nina Ortiz (CFO). Procurement lead is Priya Rao and security lead is Ravi Kumar (cc'd separately).
- Decision criteria (high level): total unit cost (we run ~5M tokens/day), latency targets for interactive features (95th %ile < 400ms), SOC2 + data residency in us-east-1, and predictable committed spend.

Questions:
1) On pricing flexibility — our procurement team will push hard on discounting for a multi-year committed plan. What is the typical range you can consider for an enterprise ARR commitment?
2) SLA: procurement will want a 99.9% availability SLA and penalties spelled out. Any constraints on accepting SLA penalties or audit clauses?
3) Security evidence: can you share SOC2 Type II and a standard security questionnaire (we'll give you ours).

Next steps: Priya (procurement) will send the initial questionnaire. Nina wants rough TCO and an estimate of committed pricing before we route to finance. Can you send a procurement checklist and a one-pager on pricing band assumptions?

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Patel
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Health

From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear summary, and great to meet Nina and Priya on the call. Short answers up front and proposed next steps below.

Pricing flexibility:
- We typically allow discounts on committed ARR; standard flexibility depends on term and commitment. For a 2–3 year committed contract at the volumes you mentioned, our typical range is 10–20% off list depending on seat/usage mix.

SLA / penalties:
- We offer an SLA for Hosted and Dedicated customers. We can discuss 99.9% availability for Dedicated commitments, but penalty language and certain audit clauses require Legal review.

Security evidence:
- SOC2 Type II is available — attaching our standard security pack and a procurement checklist (Procurement_Checklist.xlsx). Happy to run a security deep-dive with Ravi.

Attachments: Procurement_Checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), AcmeHealth_MADP_SOW_v1.pdf (draft SOW stub)

Proposed next steps: 
1) Priya to share procurement questionnaire — we'll return answers within 3 business days.
2) I'll prepare a committed pricing estimate and a short TCO model for Nina (will send by EOD Wed).
3) Loop in RevOps/Legal for any discount/SLA exceptions — tagging Jonas and Marissa here.

If you can share an expected procurement timeline that helps prioritize the approvals.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

On Thu, Feb 26, 2026 at 08:22 AM Priya Rao <priya.roa@acme-health.com> wrote:
> High level timeline: procurement review next week, finance approval the following week, legal review may add another 7–10 business days depending on redlines.

Thanks for the tag, Aditya. Quick internal take for the approval path:
- Discount authority: AE (Aditya) can approve up to 10% with RevOps (me) notification. Manager approval (Marissa) required for 11–15%. Any discount above 15% requires Director/Finance sign-off and a business case (ARR, gross margin impact).
- SLA exceptions: Legal must review any penalty or audit clauses beyond our standard terms. We can propose alternative language (service credits rather than cash penalties) to accelerate procurement acceptance.
- Security exceptions: Security will evaluate any non-standard requests; SOC2 Type II and our security pack should cover the initial questionnaire. For deep audits (on-site or vendor-specific questionnaires) Security schedules a kickoff and scope call.

Action items for Aditya:
1) Send committed pricing scenarios and the TCO summary (link to hubspot deal appreciated).
2) If procurement asks for >15% discount or specific penalty language, escalate with a brief business case (expected ARR, renewal/expansion probability).

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4827

Jonas Weber
RevOps | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-02-27T14:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Inference - Post-call recap, stakeholder mapping & procurement next steps

Aditya / Jonas — I reviewed the proposed approach. Approvals from my side:
- Discount: we can authorize up to 15% for this deal given the volume and multi-year potential. If procurement pushes for more than 15%, escalate to Finance for an exceptions review; Aditya please include ARR and expected 24-mo gross margin impact in that escalation.
- SLA: we should avoid open-ended cash penalty language. Offer service credits up to a capped monthly amount tied to committed spend; Legal to provide a standard addendum. I'll ask Legal to prioritize review if Procurement indicates SLA is a blocker.
- Security: provide the SOC2 Type II report and schedule a technical security call with Ravi. Security will triage the procurement questionnaire once we return answers.

Aditya: proceed to send the committed pricing scenarios and TCO; attach the procurement checklist and the draft SOW we discussed. If you want, I can join the procurement sync next week.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
